[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Per Crane Data Centers own site, this is a multi phase campus in Forest Grove, Oregon, near Hillsboro. PDX01 Phase 1 and Phase 2 each total 36,000 square feet of white space plus 6,400 square feet of adjacent flex space at 24 MW apiece, and PDX02 adds roughly 150,000 square feet at roughly 48 MW, for a stated campus total of more than 100 MW. PDX02 is targeted ready for service in the third quarter of 2026. No street address is published on this page, and this session could not confirm how much of PDX01 is already operating versus still under construction, so critical_it_mw is left unset rather than populated from a mixed operating and planned figure. This session made a further attempt to resolve a street address. The operators own page describes the campus only as about 8 miles from Hillsboro airport, adjacent to a regional highway, still without a street number. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned a single, 0.9 confidence candidate, 3975 Heather Street, Forest Grove, OR 97116, with no second, independent source confirming a Crane facility at that address. Given no second, independent source corroborates the geocoded address, it is not applied, consistent with this projects standard that a geocoding services own confidence score is not itself external corroboration.

reading.body:
Crane DC - Portland publishes 36,000 square feet of technical space but no IT load in megawatts, making it impossible to assess compute capacity or suitability for AI workloads that depend on power density.

Power delivery is the binding constraint for AI training clusters, and square footage alone reveals nothing about how much compute this facility can host. A 36,000 square foot data center could support 5 MW or 50 MW depending on cooling infrastructure, floor loading, and electrical distribution, none of which Crane publishes. The operator's planned campus expansion to over 100 MW across Forest Grove is substantial for Oregon, yet this specific facility remains unquantified.

The seven certifications on record, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, FISMA, NIST 800-53, HITRUST, SSAE 18, and LEED, map to regulated workloads in payments, federal systems, and healthcare rather than hyperscale training. This certification profile suggests the operator targets enterprise and government tenants, but that is inference from compliance alone. No published tenant list or workload claim confirms the facility's actual use.

The facility's place in Oregon's infrastructure remains opaque. Only six of 133 mapped Oregon data centers publish any capacity number, totaling 182 MW. Without Crane's power specification, whether this Forest Grove campus represents material new capacity for AI or serves existing regulated industries cannot be determined from available data.
